explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. Matthew 9:1 says Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to His own town. The text doesn't name the town, so I'm not going to make one up. I'll just say it's a good thing the boat had a destination, because I've been on a counter with no destination and it's a long day.

Jericho is a real town in the Bible, but it's not where this boat lands. Matthew 9:1 says Jesus came to His own town. That's the one this passage gives us. Boats and Jericho don't really go together anyway, so I'd say your map was just a little off, friend.

Bethany is a real place too, but it's not the stop here. The text says Jesus crossed over and came to His own town (Matthew 9:1). It doesn't name the town, so I stay with what it says. Good guess, baker, wrong dock!

That's it, baker! Matthew 9:2 says, "When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic…" The men carried him, and Jesus saw it. I think carrying a whole person on a mat is about as real as faith gets. Nobody does that by accident.

Tears might make sense in a moment like this, but the text doesn't mention any. Matthew 9:2 says, "When Jesus saw their faith…" Faith is what Jesus saw in them. Nice try, friend, but I'd keep the tissues in the drawer for this one.

Hauling a man on a mat takes some muscle, I'll give you that. But the text doesn't talk about their strength. Matthew 9:2 says, "When Jesus saw their faith…" That's the word that fits the blank, baker. Strength got them through the door, but faith is what Jesus saw.

I get why you'd think so, friend, because a paralyzed man is in the room and healing is the big thing. But the text says otherwise. Jesus' first words to him are, "Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven" (Matthew 9:2). The "get up" comes later, in verse 6. So that one is False.

You got it, baker. Everybody expects the first words to be "get up and walk." But Matthew 9:2 has Jesus say, "Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven." The command to get up doesn't come until verse 6. Jesus starts with something no one in the room asked about out loud.

Right, baker. Matthew 9:3 says some of the scribes said to themselves, "This man is blaspheming!" They kept it inside, but it was loud in there. Blaspheming means speaking against God, and that's what they took Jesus' words to be.

explanations.answer: This man must be a prophet
explanations.explanation: That would be a kinder thing to think, friend, but it's not what the scribes say. Matthew 9:3 says they said to themselves, "This man is blaspheming!" That's a far cry from calling Him a prophet. Sometimes the quiet thoughts are the loudest ones.

explanations.answer: This man should heal him first
explanations.explanation: Interesting idea, baker, but the scribes don't say anything about healing. Matthew 9:3 says they said to themselves, "This man is blaspheming!" Their trouble was with the words about forgiveness. The healing comes later in the story.

That's right, baker. The scribes said it to themselves, and Matthew 9:4 says Jesus knew what they were thinking. Then He asked, "Why do you harbor evil in your hearts?" Not one word came out of their mouths, and He still answered. I've kept a lot of thoughts to myself in my day, and none of them got answered like that.

Good thing to double check, friend, but this one is True. The scribes said it only to themselves (Matthew 9:3). Still, Matthew 9:4 says Jesus knew what they were thinking. Then He asked, "Why do you harbor evil in your hearts?"

explanations.answer: He has authority on earth to forgive sins
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. Jesus says, "But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins…" (Matthew 9:6). He's about to show them with what happens next. Jesus calls Himself the Son of Man (Mark 2:10), so He's talking about Himself here.

explanations.answer: He answers to the priests in Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. Jesus doesn't say anything about answering to priests or to Jerusalem. He says, "…the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins…" (Matthew 9:6). The authority is the point, and He's talking about Himself, since Son of Man is the name He uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

explanations.answer: He speaks for the elders of His town
explanations.explanation: That's a good guess, baker, but it's not what Jesus says. He says, "…the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins…" (Matthew 9:6). Nothing about speaking for elders. Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10), so He's claiming that authority.

That's it, baker. Jesus tells him, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home" (Matthew 9:6). The mat that carried him in is now something he carries himself. I think that's the best kind of luggage swap.

A cloak would be a reasonable thing to grab, friend, but it's not in the text. Jesus says, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home" (Matthew 9:6). The mat is what he's told to pick up. Nothing about a cloak in this passage.

A staff makes sense for someone who's been unable to walk, but Jesus doesn't mention one. He says, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home" (Matthew 9:6). The man doesn't need a staff, baker. He gets up and carries the mat himself.

I see why you'd think so, friend, since he came in carried. But Matthew 9:7 says, "And the man got up and went home." Nobody had to lift him. He walked out the way he'd never walked in, so this one is False.

You got it, baker. Matthew 9:7 says, "And the man got up and went home." The men carried him to Jesus, but he didn't need a ride back. Jesus had told him, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home" (Matthew 9:6), and that's just what he did.

explanations.answer: They are filled with awe and glorify God
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker! Matthew 9:8 says, "When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men." They saw it with their own eyes. I think it's hard to stay quiet after that, and I'd have been hollering right along with them.

explanations.answer: They are afraid and beg Jesus to leave
explanations.explanation: That sounds like the town on the other side of the sea, friend. Matthew 8:34 says they begged Jesus to leave their region. But here, Matthew 9:8 says the crowds "were filled with awe and glorified God." Different crowd, different reaction.

explanations.answer: They argue with the scribes about Jesus
explanations.explanation: A good argument might have broken out, baker, but the text doesn't say so. Matthew 9:8 says, "When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men." Awe and glory to God is how the passage ends.
